title: Flowers of Crystal
build: TOSEC disc, Flowers of Crystal (1984)(4Mat).ssd (SHA-256 0f591a69...57d0), a 40-track DFS disc of eight BBC BASIC II programs and four files of machine code; each program analysed as CHAIN loads it at &1900, the two adventures' machine code where their sound programs load it

Lines 1-2, as in part 1: loaded at &1900, line 1 sends the program to lines 32220-32225, which copy it down to &0E00 and RUN it; run there, line 2 clears the variables and puts the REM token (244) over line 1's IF at &0E04.

Lines 3-4, REMs: `(C) 4MAT 1984` and `MIKE MATSON` after bell characters and a green code; the character 21 at the end of line 4 switches the VDU off when the program is LISTed, so a listing stops showing after these two lines.

Lines 5-6: a text window of one character (VDU 28,0,0,0,0), the code of f0 put in the keyboard buffer (*FX138,0,128), and STOP. At the prompt the MOS types f0's definition, set by N2: `DELETE1,6`, `32220` and `32225` remove the loader's lines, then MODE 7 and RUN.
Line 10: ON ERROR GOTO 32000, which sets A% to 0 and RUNs: an error or SHIFT-f0's ESCAPE starts part 2 again at The Face, with nothing held.

Line 50, strings: the characters allowed in answers (Z$ letters and space, N$ digits, M$ `123`, O$ `12`, YN$ `YESyesNOno`), the four rows of the white bubble (b1$-b4$), and a toadstool's red cap (t$) and yellow stalk (s$) for the Exiles' game.
Line 90: the screen cleared (PROCc), print format @% set to 0, paged mode off (VDU 15) and the cursor off (VDU 23,0,10,32).

Line 100. s%(1-20), the state of each spell: 0 not held, 1 held, 2 used; ds$(1-9), words of a description; v%, the ground's profile and the Exiles' columns; w%, the Exiles' rows; m% and n%, the toadstools'. zz% is set and never read. On a fresh start (A%=0) Z%, the place, becomes 1, The Face, and S% and T%, the spells packed as bits, and F%, L%, O%, W%, E% and R%, the six parts of the flower dream, are cleared.

Lines 1000-1010, one visit to a place. The spells are unpacked from S% and T% into s%() (PROCspre); unless this is the very start or Z% is 7, half the time a description of the surroundings (PROCde). Then the place's function is called by name, EVAL("FNL"+STR$(Z%)), FNL1 to FNL10, the spells are packed again (PROCspst), and RUN starts the next visit: only A% to Z% carry anything from one to the next.

FNi(l,in$,h,x,y,Q), lines 2005-2090, an answer typed by the player: as part 1's, without the capitals: magenta lines above and below (PROCv), the colour Q+128, dots for l characters, and the keys in in$ accepted, each letter made lower case, DELETE taking one back and anything else beeping (VDU 7). RETURN gives back what was typed.

FNL1, lines 3500-3590, The Face. A yellow screen, the face drawn by PROCfc, red edges, and a panel for its words on rows 16-24. On a fresh start PROCfc is given 6 and the face forms out of coloured dust; later it is given 0 and appears at once. The first visit (A%=0) runs the questions at line 3700, sets A% to 6 and goes to the Globs (Z%=5); every later visit runs line 3800 and goes to Rumala's Row (Z%=2).

Lines 3700-3745, The Face's first words: `So! Another foolish person comes to challenge the powers of Rumala! I am The Face, made from the dust of the earth and the smoke of the air.`, then `How old are you?` (three digits). Under 197, `You are much too young.`; over, `much too old.`; either way the function ends and the RUN brings The Face back. At 197, `You are the same age as I am.`, the six parts of the flower dream to find, the Flower to be brought to its castle, and five special spells.
